title: Replace repository-root selection with reusable Git resolution
objective: Completely replace configuration-based repository-root selection with a reusable Git-backed repository-root component that commands and core code can consume consistently, while keeping the installed schema registry separate and continuing to resolve schemas through schema-validate.

branch.name: WI-0035-git-repository-root
branch.rationale: Repository-root selection affects every repository-dependent command and must be implemented, reviewed, and validated on a dedicated context branch before primary-branch release.

request.text: sdlc should be resolving the repository root using git. Prepare a new work item to completely replace the current repository root resolution logic and replace it with using git to resolve the repository root. This should be a component that commands/code/etc can reference easily. Commit the work item.

scope.name: git-repository-root-component
scope.description: Add one reusable Git-backed repository-root resolver that accepts a starting path or current working directory, invokes Git safely, normalizes the root, and exposes stable diagnostics/context for consumers.
scope.reason: Repository-dependent commands currently duplicate root assumptions and fall back to one global configured repository.

scope.name: repository-context-migration
scope.description: Route configuration, operative-root helpers, command context, repository-dependent commands, validation, references, migrations, branch checks, and hooks through the shared Git-root component.
scope.reason: A reusable component is only effective when all repository-content operations use the same selection boundary.

scope.name: schema-registry-separation
scope.description: Keep repositoryRoot exclusively for target repository content and Git operations; keep schemaRegistryRoot exclusively for the installed schema registry and schema-validate --root/--schema resolution.
scope.reason: External repositories must validate against the installed registry without requiring a schemas directory in the target repository.

scope.name: configuration-and-installer-removal
scope.description: Remove the singleton ~/.sdlc/config.json repositoryRoot fallback and update install/config behavior so installing one repository cannot silently select it for unrelated repositories.
scope.reason: A single global repositoryRoot does not support multiple repositories on one machine and can target the wrong repository outside Git.

scope.name: multi-repository-validation
scope.description: Add isolated tests for nested paths, sibling repositories, non-repository directories, explicit path overrides, worktrees, Git errors, schema registry separation, installer behavior, and every migrated command family.
scope.reason: The reported failure is a cross-repository selection defect and requires end-to-end evidence.

nonGoals.name: schema-registry-relocation
nonGoals.description: Do not move or duplicate the installed schema registry into target repositories and do not make repositoryRoot determine schema-validate resolution.
nonGoals.reason: schemaRegistryRoot and schema-validate are separate package-owned schema concerns.

nonGoals.name: arbitrary-repository-selection
nonGoals.description: Do not silently select a configured or unrelated repository when Git cannot resolve a root; require an explicit path/profile mechanism for outside-repository operation.
nonGoals.reason: Ambiguous repository selection is unsafe on machines containing multiple repositories.

nonGoals.name: command-business-semantics
nonGoals.description: Do not change command business behavior, output schemas, reference syntax, migration semantics, task identifiers, or schema contract meaning beyond root-selection diagnostics and wiring.
nonGoals.reason: This work item changes repository context resolution rather than domain command semantics.

nonGoals.name: remote-publication
nonGoals.description: Do not publish packages, deploy, or push remote branches/tags as part of implementation or validation; release remains a bounded local primary-branch task.
nonGoals.reason: Local repository-root evidence does not establish external deployment or publication.

items.name: git-root-authority
items.description: The authoritative repository-root resolver must use Git to resolve the nearest repository root from an explicit starting path or current working directory and must not use ~/.sdlc/config.json repositoryRoot as a content-root fallback.
items.reason: Git defines repository membership and handles nested directories, worktrees, and repository layout more reliably than a singleton user configuration value.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A path inside a Git repository resolves to the normalized Git top-level root, including from nested directories and files.
A non-repository path returns a stable actionable error and never silently selects another configured repository.
The resolver supports explicit path input, current-working-directory fallback, Git worktrees, and safe Git command failure handling.

items.name: shared-repository-context
items.description: Commands and core code must consume one reusable repository-root/context component instead of independently resolving or inferring repository roots.
items.reason: One policy boundary is required for consistent behavior across CLI commands, validation, references, migrations, branch checks, and hooks.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Repository-dependent command modules receive or call the shared resolver and no longer use a singleton configured repositoryRoot fallback.
Repository content operations, Git operations, relative-path calculations, and target reports use the same resolved root and preserve existing output contracts.

items.name: schema-registry-separation
items.description: Schema validation must use the installed schema registry through schema-validate, with schemaRegistryRoot independent of repositoryRoot.
items.reason: Target repositories may not contain schemas; schema-validate must resolve registered schemas from the installed registry rather than the target repository.

acceptanceCriteria.description: schema-validate invocations receive schemaRegistryRoot as --root and schema paths are resolved within that registry.
Reference-schema discovery and validation do not read repositoryRoot/schemas when validating an external target repository.
Reports continue to identify target repository paths separately from schema registry paths.

items.name: installer-configuration-safety
items.description: scripts/install.mjs and configuration resolution must stop treating one ~/.sdlc/config.json repositoryRoot value as the universal repository selection mechanism.
items.reason: Installing repository B must not leave repository A as an implicit fallback for outside-repository commands.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Installer behavior is idempotent and multi-repository-safe: installing one repository cannot silently overwrite or claim to register a different repository selection.
Outside-repository invocation requires an explicit target/profile or fails with actionable guidance rather than selecting a stale singleton repositoryRoot.

items.name: complete-root-resolution-evidence
items.description: The change must have focused implementation/review tests, full package gates, external-repository validation, and a bounded release record before consumer adoption is considered.
items.reason: Repository-root selection is a cross-cutting infrastructure boundary whose regression can affect every command.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Tests cover at least two repositories, nested CWDs, non-repository paths, explicit selection, worktrees, stale config, installed registry schemas, and representative repository-dependent commands.
Typecheck, build, complete tests, schema audit, work-item validation, and release gates pass with no unresolved references.

versionSuggestion.rationale: Replaces public repository-root selection and configuration behavior with a reusable Git-backed component while preserving command semantics and separately retaining schema-registry resolution.
versionSuggestion.disclaimer: This is an inferred recommendation; increase the impact if final changes introduce breaking command behavior or alter the public configuration contract beyond the planned replacement.
